comparisons.peer_summary: Products may be subject to security vulnerabilities that could have a material adverse effect on the business.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD explicitly disclose that security vulnerabilities in their products could have a material adverse effect on their business. QCOM broadens this to include product defects and errors, noting an adverse impact on customers and end users, while AMD specifically isolates product security vulnerabilities as a distinct risk factor leading to material adverse effects.

sentences.text: Accordingly, defects, errors or security vulnerabilities in our products or the technologies we use could have an adverse impact on us, on our customers and the end users of our customers' products.
If any of these risks materialize, there could be a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
◦Our products may be subject to security vulnerabilities that could have a material adverse effect on us.

peer_results.rationale: AVGO candidates focus on cybersecurity threats to IT systems and software infrastructure management (avgo_2024_1A_D006, avgo_2024_1A_D017). While related to security, these disclosures concern the integrity of internal IT infrastructure and vendor systems rather than defects, errors, or security vulnerabilities within the company's actual products sold to customers, which is the specific focus of the QCOM disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Product Security Vulnerabilities and Operational Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces risks from security vulnerabilities in its processors and third-party components, including side-channel variants like Spectre and Meltdown. Mitigations may be untimely or ineffective, and export restrictions can hinder patch deployment. These vulnerabilities can lead to significant costs for updates, litigation, and regulatory responses, damage reputation, and reduce product demand, especially if competitors' products are more secure. Premature public disclosure of vulnerabilities can exacerbate these risks.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify security vulnerabilities in their products as a material risk. QCOM states generally that defects, errors, or security vulnerabilities could have a material adverse effect. INTC provides a more granular comparison by specifying that these vulnerabilities occur in processors, third-party components, and associated operating systems/workloads, and can lead to performance issues, data loss, or reputational damage, ultimately adversely affecting results of operations and financial condition.

sentences.text: Accordingly, defects, errors or security vulnerabilities in our products or the technologies we use could have an adverse impact on us, on our customers and the end users of our customers' products.
If any of these risks materialize, there could be a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
We face risks related to security vulnerabilities in our products.

We or third parties regularly identify security vulnerabilities with respect to our processors and other products, as well as the operating systems and workloads that run on them and the components that interact with them.

Security vulnerabilities and any limitations or adverse effects of mitigation techniques can adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition, customer relationships, prospects, and reputation in a number of ways, any of which may be material.

peer_results.rationale: MU candidates focus on the risk of unsuccessful technology development (mu_2024_1A_D025) and intellectual property protection failure (mu_2024_1A_D045). These are distinct from the risk of product defects, errors, or security vulnerabilities in existing products that could have a material adverse effect, as described by QCOM.

comparisons.peer_summary: Complex hardware and software offerings, including AI products using third-party training data, contain risks of defects, security vulnerabilities, and failures that may lead to significant warranty expenses, remediation costs, and legal liabilities, as evidenced by a 2023 Data Center component defect.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVDA group product defects and security vulnerabilities as sources of potential material adverse effects. QCOM broadly states that defects, errors, or security vulnerabilities in products or technologies could have an adverse impact. NVDA elaborates that defects, security vulnerabilities, or failures in complex hardware/software (including AI products) can lead to loss of market acceptance, withdrawal from products, and negative impacts on financial results and reputation.

They have in the past and may in the future contain defects or security vulnerabilities or experience failures or unsatisfactory performance due to any number of issues in design, fabrication, packaging, materials, bugs and/or use within a system.
